Replay

Replaying recorded network simulation

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Scrapyard integrationLarge-model WASM verificationOlder network recordings

Use net.recording_model(&model) to verify recorded network simulation without opening a session or replaying transport traffic. The adapter supplies the engine-free recording verifier with a network Model(State, Control, Action, Event, Seats). The recorded input type is Batch(Control, Action, Seats) and the event type is Net_Event(Event), matching the simulation run by server and client timelines.

Odin
archive: d.Recording(World, net.Batch(Control, Action, SEATS), net.Net_Event(Event))
defer d.recording_destroy(&archive)
identity := d.Recording_Context{content = CONTENT, build = MODEL_REVISION, tick_hz = 60}
result := d.recording_capture(&archive, &server.timeline, identity)
// Encode/persist, or decode a file into a fresh recording owner.
model := game.model()
capture: r.Audit_Capture(World, net.Batch(Control, Action, SEATS), net.Net_Event(Event))
defer r.audit_capture_destroy(&capture)
checked := d.recording_verify(&archive, identity, net.recording_model(&model), &capture)

Keep model and its immutable user data alive at a stable address throughout verification. The adapter preflights all recorded controls, seat masks, prediction group/seat identifiers, view shapes, action sequences and executable action payloads before any simulation step. The optional Recording_Model.input_check(input, tick, user) supplies context-aware preflight without changing existing models that use input_valid or neither callback.

Batches already record joins, leaves, fresh-seat resets, controls, aim brackets, actions, sequence IDs and admission rejections. Verification runs the ordinary network simulation reducer, including action rollback and result occurrences. It does not rerun admission callbacks, action scheduling, transport, snapshots, lease checks or presentation. Previously accepted actions remain eligible for replay even if today's live admission policy would reject them. Recorded rejected requests remain rejected; their semantically invalid payloads never reach the game's action predicate. Rejected view hints likewise remain diagnostic data.

Client recordings preserve the replayable prediction suffix after the latest correction. They may therefore be much shorter than the authority recording. A captured client value may contain projection defaults in private fields because the authority never sent their contents. Verify it with the matching model and prediction policy. The recording cannot recover data absent from that client's received view.

An archive can be verified after destroying every transport/session object. It contains simulation evidence, not a restorable network session: credentials, transport queues, replay authorization, durable admission and coordinator leases are not reconstructed. Checksums and successful replay do not prove that a file originated from a trusted authority. Model/build identity remains the application's explicit compatibility contract.

Scrapyard integration#

With RSY_DEV=1, the separate Replay Scrapyard game adds Export recording after Save in its Escape menu. It exports the authority timeline on solo/host/ server, or the local prediction suffix on a client. Ordinary launches add no recording control. Native output defaults to user://scrapyard.rplrec and can be overridden by RSY_RECORDING_PATH; Chrome requests a file download.

The operation is synchronous and does not pause the network game. Complete world and batch copies make it useful for deliberate debugging, not every-frame capture. The codec limits remain 16 MiB per file, 1 MiB per chunk and 64 MiB of owned record values. Export logs include the range, bytes, storage result and elapsed microseconds. Those timings do not by themselves show that the network game continued without resynchronization; that behavior needs separate evidence.

Shell
nix develop --command odin run examples/replay_scrapyard/tools/verify_recording \
  -collection:godot="$PWD" -- /absolute/path/scrapyard.rplrec

The tool uses the same Scrapyard model, carried catalog/rules and explicit manual recording revision. It reports complete replay agreement, action verdict counts, historical-view samples and gameplay counters, or the first mismatch field. The original Kit game and its save/recovery formats remain independent.

Large-model WASM verification#

Several simultaneous aggregate copies in recording_verify formerly generated 77,660 locals for Scrapyard, exceeding V8's limit. Verification now borrows retained entries and copies complete fixed-value failure frames into disjoint owned storage with mem.copy_non_overlapping. Logical comparison, capture ownership and canonical file bytes are unchanged; padding is never serialized as gameplay state.

The standalone Scrapyard WASM verifier links Emscripten's math library, including single-precision sine/cosine, just as the web toolchain supplies those routines. Its final module has no imported functions; the simulation does not run in a JS surrogate. tests/replay_network_recording/targets.sh builds this target and verifies actual native/browser exports, corruption, recomputed-checksum state mismatches and invalid-input preflight. This is evidence for the recorded workloads, not universal floating-point determinism across operating systems or all scenarios.

Older network recordings#

Recorded authority observations add a field to Batch. This changes diagnostic input fingerprints even for models with the authority policy disabled. Gameplay packet/checkpoint formats remain separate. Normal decode rejects older input schemas; it does not silently assume missing observations.

For an unchanged model with its authority policy disabled, net.recording_upgrade_without_authority explicitly converts the prior Batch schema, retaining recording context, complete frames, controls, action decisions and events. Enabled authority policies are refused because the old data cannot supply the required observations. Structural conversion does not certify replay agreement; run the verifier on the resulting file.

Scrapyard provides a bounded converter that requires a new destination:

Shell
nix develop --command odin run examples/replay_scrapyard/tools/upgrade_recording \
  -collection:godot="$PWD" -- old.rplrec converted.rplrec
nix develop --command odin run examples/replay_scrapyard/tools/verify_recording \
  -collection:godot="$PWD" -- converted.rplrec

The converter leaves its source intact and refuses to replace existing files or symlinks. It publishes the destination through a temporary file in the same directory and a hard link. Three earlier native/browser recordings have been converted and verified against their complete recorded state/event sequences.

Scrapyard content 48 recordings#

The Scrapyard format-only upgrade_recording tool remains specific to content 48. It adds the formerly absent authority-observation field with an unknown value; it does not relabel historical gameplay as content 49. Verify its output with:

Shell
/path/to/verify_recording /path/to/converted.rplrec --content48

The explicit legacy model retains the old world schema and disabled authority policy. Its ordinary gameplay callbacks are unchanged between contents 48 and 49; future gameplay revisions must preserve that historical implementation separately. Current content-49 recordings use the verifier without this flag. Checkpoint conversion is a different operation: it seeds the prior authority epoch so future recovery can apply the new timer policy.
